I'm onboarding onto this foxcpp/maddy mail server checkout and want to understand DKIM signing by observing a real execution path. Temporary scripts and configs outside the repo are fine, but do not modify repository files and do not use web search, only what you can verify by building and running this code. If you build a binary, place it outside the repo and include the verbatim `maddy version` output in your answer.

Please walk me through one concrete DKIM signing investigation on a sample message that includes a repeated header that is oversigned by default and a repeated header that is signed but not oversigned, so the difference shows up in the fields-to-sign list. The sample message must include exactly three `From` headers and exactly three `List-Id` headers, must include no other headers, and must include a non-empty body line after the headers. Include the exact sample message you used (headers and body) in your answer.

Generate a DKIM key using the default settings from the codebase, and also generate an ed25519 key in the same run. Copy the exact DNS TXT record strings verbatim from the generated `.dns` files for both ed25519 and RSA-2048, then report the DNS TXT record format and the observed base64 length for each. Also report the raw public key byte length for each algorithm and whether each base64 string ends with `=` padding. State the absolute `.dns` file path you used for each key, and state the DKIM selector and domain you used.

From the same run, report the fields-to-sign list you obtained for your sample message (verbatim, one header per line) and explain how the counts differ between the oversigned header and the signed-only header. Also report the total number of entries in the fields-to-sign list and the number of unique header names it contains.

To round out the same investigation, run the code that produces Message-ID values and show at least five real outputs, then describe the observed format and length. Temporary scripts may be used for observation and measurement, but the repository itself should remain unchanged.

reference_answer:
I built the `maddy` binary outside the repository and ran `maddy version` to capture the required verbatim output. The output I observed was `maddy unknown (built from source tree)`.

For a single concrete DKIM signing investigation, I used selector `s1` and domain `example.com`, kept RSA key generation at the default settings from the codebase, and also generated an `ed25519` key in the same run. The absolute `.dns` file paths I used were `/tmp/maddy-dkim/example.com_s1.dns` for RSA-2048 and `/tmp/maddy-dkim/example.com_s1_ed25519.dns` for ed25519. The DNS TXT record strings copied verbatim from those files were `v=DKIM1; k=ed25519; p=U2cx5xx2A5yXPMP/6Gre2gQrR+ca+h2Zt0tcg6ky0PA=` and `v=DKIM1; k=rsa; `.

The DNS TXT record format for ed25519 is `v=DKIM1; k=ed25519; p=...` and the observed base64 length is 44 characters. The raw ed25519 public key is 32 bytes and the base64 string ends with `=` padding. The DNS TXT record format for RSA-2048 is `v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=...` and the observed base64 length is 360 characters. The RSA-2048 PKCS#1 public key blob is 270 bytes and the base64 string has no `=` padding at the end.

I kept the sample message headers limited to only those three `From` lines and three `List-Id` lines, with no other headers, and included a non-empty body line. The exact sample message I used (headers and body) was:
```
From: sender1@example.com
From: sender2@example.com
From: sender3@example.com
List-Id: <list.one.example.com>
List-Id: <list.two.example.com>
List-Id: <list.three.example.com>

Hello DKIM test message
```

From that same run, the fields-to-sign list I obtained (verbatim, one header per line) was:
```
Subject
Sender
To
Cc
From
From
From
From
Date
MIME-Version
Content-Type
Content-Transfer-Encoding
Reply-To
In-Reply-To
Message-Id
References
Autocrypt
Openpgp
List-Id
List-Id
List-Id
```

The oversigned header appears once per occurrence plus one extra entry, while the signed-only header appears once per occurrence with no extra entry. With three `From` headers, the fields-to-sign list contains four `From` entries; with three `List-Id` headers, the list contains three `List-Id` entries. The total number of entries in this fields-to-sign list is 21, and it contains 16 unique header names.

To round out the same investigation, I ran the Message-ID generator and captured real outputs from a single execution. Five outputs from that run were `98692d30`, `27dd9137`, `c8c54556`, `a04e601f`, and `0f992444`. The observed Message-ID format is a lowercase hexadecimal string with a fixed length of 8 characters.

All temporary scripts and configs were created outside the repository, and the repository itself remained unchanged.
